candidate_relations.label: Small-bowel intussusception
candidate_relations.reason: In a 17-year-old with a right hypochondrial abdominal mass, severe anaemia (Hb 4 g/dL), low-grade fever, and imaging showing small-bowel intussusception, the clinical picture is most consistent with Burkitt lymphoma as the underlying cause. Burkitt lymphoma is the commonest cause of intussusception in older children and adolescents in endemic regions, and the mass with these systemic features points to a lymphomatous lead point. The reference diagnosis is Burkitt lymphoma; small-bowel intussusception is the radiological/mechanical manifestation rather than the final aetiological diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Intussusception is the mechanical complication/presentation caused by the underlying Burkitt lymphoma acting as a lead point; it is not the primary diagnostic entity requested

case_quality_flags: Severe anaemia (Hb 4 g/dL) and age >10 years strongly favour a pathological lead point (Burkitt lymphoma) over idiopathic intussusception
Endemic Burkitt lymphoma context implied by clinical profile; HIV negativity noted
